sources.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), 91 printed pages
sources.locator: Sections 2.1-2.5, 3.1-3.2, 4.1-4.4 and 5.1-5.6; equations (2.1)-(2.40), (3.1)-(3.3), (4.1)-(4.94) and the torus energy estimates of Section 3.1; printed pp. 6-31, 42-56, 62-91

contents.name: Section 2.4, The Evolution Equations: gauge source functions, the harmonically reduced field equations (2.39) and the subsidiary system
contents.support: The definition fixes the gauge vector, the reduced equation and the residual; the residual identity and the subsidiary wave equation are proved in lem-gr-einstein-residual-and-subsidiary-identity.

contents.name: Section 3.1, Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems: definition, finite-dimensional approximation, energy and Moser estimates, uniqueness, compactness and passage to a classical solution, Remarks 1-6 (smooth persistence, continuation, Cauchy stability, non-identity time matrix)
contents.support: The whole E0 chain (Galerkin projection, estimates, compactness, limit, persistence, uniqueness/stability) is authored locally with complete proofs; the source supplies the method and the statement but not the lettering. The higher-order time-continuity estimate and the locally uniform extraction used in the limit passage are authored as lem-gr-galerkin-second-time-derivative-bound and lem-gr-rational-diagonal-extraction.

contents.name: Section 3.2, Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems on Manifolds: invariant definition and localisation
contents.support: The packaged well-posedness theorem and the finite-speed independence lemma state the manifold-local form.

contents.name: Section 4.2, The Einstein-Euler System: hyperbolic reduction of the perfect fluid, specific enthalpy and sound-speed conditions (4.38), and the pressure-free (dust) subsidiary system, equations (4.26)-(4.48) and (4.56)-(4.63)
contents.support: The barotropic enthalpy-variable lemma and the complete dust chain (variables, Weyl reconstruction, reduced evolution, subsidiary vanishing, tilted initialisation) are authored locally; the source is the derivation provenance for the reduction equations.

contents.name: Section 5.1, Local Existence Theorems for the Einstein Equations: harmonic-map gauge, reduced initial data, propagation of the gauge and local existence
contents.support: The local development, reduced existence and constraint propagation items reproduce the argument in the local-coordinate form used by the page.

contents.name: Section 5.2, Uniqueness: geometric uniqueness up to diffeomorphism
contents.support: The page proves geometric uniqueness by putting two developments into a common harmonic-map gauge and invoking reduced uniqueness.

contents.name: Section 5.4, Matter Models: definition of a matter model and scalar-field matter
contents.support: The scalar reduction lemma and the scalar local-evolution theorem verify the matter hypotheses of the abstract development theorem.

contents.name: Section 5.5, An Example of an Ill-Posed Initial Value Problem: relativistic Euler equations with p=k rho, k<0, and the explicit growing Fourier modes
contents.support: The counterexample proves the failure of fixed-Sobolev local existence for p'<0, following the source's mode computation.

contents.name: Section 2.1, The Principal Symbol; Section 2.2, symmetric hyperbolic systems; Section 2.3, characteristics
contents.support: The principal-symbol and characteristic notions are absorbed into the definitions and reduction lemmas rather than given standalone items.

contents.name: Section 4.1, Hyperbolic Systems from the ADM Equations
contents.reason: The page uses the harmonic-gauge reduction, not the ADM-based hyperbolic systems; the ADM evolution system belongs to the 3+1 formulation material of earlier GR pages.

contents.name: Section 4.3, The Initial Boundary Value Problem
contents.reason: The page treats the pure Cauchy problem on a spacelike surface with no timelike boundary; initial-boundary value problems are outside the assigned Gr14 scope.

contents.name: Section 4.4, The Einstein-Dirac System
contents.reason: Fermionic matter is not one of the selected matter sectors (vacuum, scalar, strict barotropic fluid, geodesic dust) of this batch.

contents.name: Section 5.3, Cauchy Stability and Section 5.6, Symmetries
contents.support: The continuous-dependence estimate of the periodic theorem supplies the Cauchy-stability content used by the page; symmetry inheritance is not needed for the local development claims and is not authored here.

contents.name: Section 1, Introduction and overview
contents.reason: Overview and historical material carries no separately built mathematical result; the substantive statements are harvested from the sections above.

sources.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007), 189 printed pages
sources.locator: Sections 2.5 (Gauss-Codazzi relations), 4.1-4.4 (3+1 decomposition and the constraint equations (4.65)-(4.66)) and 10.3.2 (Propagation of the constraints); printed pp. 61-79 and 375-380

contents.name: Section 2.5, Gauss-Codazzi relations: Gauss, Codazzi-Mainardi and Ricci equations
contents.support: The theorem proves the Gauss and Codazzi equations and the normal projections in the same sign conventions.

contents.name: Section 4.2-4.3, constraint equations (4.65)-(4.66) and the extrinsic curvature of a slice
contents.support: The metric jet of a spacelike slice and the Hamiltonian/momentum form of the constraints are used in the initial-data construction and in the constraint theorem.

contents.name: Section 10.3.2, Propagation of the constraints
contents.support: The propagation statement is proved locally for the harmonic reduction; the source's ADM discussion supplies the context only, not the proof.

contents.name: Chapters 6-10, conformal decomposition and numerical evolution
contents.reason: Conformal initial-data methods and numerical evolution are not part of the Gr14 analytic local-existence kernel.

sources.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis lecture notes), Chapter 1-8, 240 printed pages
sources.locator: Chapter 3 (Sections 3.1, 3.4, 3.5, 3.7-3.8, 3.10), Section 5.C, Section 6.4, Chapter 7 and Chapter 8; printed pp. 47-89, 172-173, 181-194 and 211-234

contents.name: Chapter 3, Sobolev spaces: weak derivatives, properties, Sobolev embedding and compactness
contents.support: The torus embedding/compactness items are proved in Fourier form; the source supports the Euclidean background and the compactness methodology. The torus compact-embedding clause and the diagonal extraction are authored as lem-gr-galerkin-compactness and lem-gr-rational-diagonal-extraction.

contents.name: Section 5.C, The Sobolev spaces H^s(R^n)
contents.support: The H^s norm conventions and Fourier characterisation are adapted to the torus and proved locally.

contents.name: Section 6.4, The Galerkin approximation
contents.support: The finite-dimensional Galerkin scheme and its ODE step are authored in Fourier form with complete proofs.

contents.name: Chapter 7, Hyperbolic Equations and Chapter 8, Friedrich symmetric systems
contents.support: The symmetric-hyperbolic existence and uniqueness theory is proved locally on the torus; the source supplies the standard hyperbolic background.

contents.name: Chapters 2, 4 and 5 (elliptic and parabolic theory, heat/Schrodinger equations)
contents.reason: Elliptic and parabolic equations play no role in the hyperbolic local-existence kernel of this page.

sources.title: M. E. Taylor, Fourier Analysis, Distributions, and Constant-Coefficient Linear PDE (UNC lecture notes, 2018)
sources.locator: Section 1 (Fourier series on the torus T^n), equations (1.1)-(1.21), covering the characters, Fourier coefficients, the Parseval identity and coefficient convergence; printed pp. 1-30

contents.name: Section 1, Fourier series on T^n: characters, Fourier coefficients, Parseval identity and inversion
contents.support: The torus measure, characters and coefficient conventions follow the source; the periodic differentiation and norm-equivalence lemma is proved locally on top of the quoted Parseval supplier.

contents.name: Section 3, The Fourier transform; Sections 4-10, distributions and constant-coefficient PDE
contents.reason: The page works entirely on the compact torus with periodic Fourier series; Euclidean Fourier transforms and distributional solution theory are not used.

sources.title: E. Wiedemann (ed. J. Skipper), Lecture Notes: Navier-Stokes Equations (Universitat Ulm, WS 2018/19)
sources.locator: Section 2.1 (Fourier characterisation of H^s(T^3), the embedding H^s(T^3) subset L-infinity for s>3/2 and the Banach-algebra property) and Section 4.3 (Agmon's inequality, Lemma 4.13); printed pp. 3-9 and 31-34

contents.name: Section 2.1, Fourier characterisation of Sobolev spaces on T^3 and the Banach-algebra property for s>3/2
contents.support: The torus algebra and embedding items prove the product and embedding bounds in the same Fourier normalisation; the source is the primary treatment for the torus statements. Completeness of the weighted coefficient space (hence of H^s(T^3)) is authored as lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-completeness.

contents.name: Section 4.3, Agmon's inequality (Lemma 4.13)
contents.support: The Agmon-type L-infinity control is absorbed into the C^m embedding and Holder bounds rather than given a separate item.

contents.name: Sections 3-5, Navier-Stokes and Euler existence theory
contents.reason: The fluid existence theory of the source is for incompressible/compressible Euler and Navier-Stokes systems on the torus, not for the Einstein-Euler system; only the torus Sobolev toolbox is harvested.

sources.title: I. Rodnianski and J. Speck, The Stability of the Irrotational Euler-Einstein System with a Positive Cosmological Constant, arXiv:0911.5501 (v2, 2010)
sources.locator: Sections 1 (introduction and formulation) and 3 (Euler-Einstein formulation and sound-speed hypotheses), including Postulate (4) 0<c_s<1 and the sound-cone discussion; printed pp. 1-20 and 30-45

contents.name: Section 1 and Section 3, Euler-Einstein formulation: speed of sound 0<c_s<1, sound cone, and the hyperbolic character of the fluid equations
contents.support: The sound-speed hypotheses and the principal-symbol positivity of the barotropic reduction are used in the fluid lemma and its worked symbol computation.

contents.name: Section 5 and later sections, energy estimates and global future stability of FLRW
contents.reason: The page proves only local existence for a strict barotropic fluid; global nonlinear stability of the FLRW family is far beyond the assigned scope.
